role: Extension on WorkoutStatsCards holding the post-workout summary's headline derived values (pace, max speed, peak HR, cadence, best split, METs, calories), the time-series chart cards (HR with zone bands, pace, power, cadence, elevation) and the heart-rate-recovery banner/card; plus file-scope helpers and static elevation/provenance helpers forwarded to the share sheet.
types: WorkoutStatsCards: extension — derived values and card builders
WorkoutStatsCards: extension — static pure helpers elevationSeries / hrrProvenanceLabel
state: static let WorkoutStatsCards.hrrCaptureWindowSec = 120 (also read by AppFactResolver+LiveNavigation.swift:818)
toplevel: Imports Charts, CoreLocation, MapKit, MessageUI, SwiftUI (MapKit and MessageUI are unused by anything in this file). Declares three static lets (120 s HRR capture window, 30 s write grace, 15 s HR-at-stop window) and three file-private free functions (distanceScale, elevationMarks, hrrNarrativeText).

flags.text: hrrCaptureWindowSec = 120 must match the recorder's independent literal captureWindowSec: 120 passed to HRRCaptureService; changing one without the other makes the countdown banner/chip disagree with the real capture window.

units.does: Active workout seconds for this session: WorkoutActiveTime.seconds over workoutMetadata.samples with session.duration (wall clock) as fallback.

flags.text: Only used by avgPaceDisplay (tests-only caller) and estimatedCaloriesDisplay (no callers); not reached by any production view.

units.does: Formats integer seconds as 'H:MM:SS' when ≥ 1 h, else 'M:SS'.

branches.effect: true: returns '%d:%02d:%02d'; false: returns '%d:%02d' (minutes not zero-padded).

flags.text: Only callers are ViewSnapshotTests.testDerivedDisplayStrings (EmuquTests/ViewSnapshotTests.swift:188-190); grep finds no production call (other formatDuration matches are different functions).
Same H:MM:SS / M:SS formatting is re-implemented in FitnessPostSummaryView.heroDurationLabel, which is what production shows.

units.does: Average pace string = activeDuration / workoutMetadata.distanceMeters, formatted per units preference (e.g. '6:12 /km'); nil when distance ≤ 100 m or active duration ≤ 10 s or either missing.
reads: ud:fitness.unitsPreference (App Group suite SharedUserDefaults.appGroup, legacy .standard fallback)

branches.cond: distanceMeters present and > 100, activeDuration present and > 10 s
branches.effect: false: returns nil; true: returns UnitsPreference.formatPace(elapsedSec:distanceMeters:) (itself nil if distance ≤ 50 / elapsed ≤ 10, unreachable here).

flags.text: Only caller is ViewSnapshotTests.testDerivedDisplayStrings; the production hero uses heroPaceLabel, which duplicates this logic with session.duration (wall clock incl. pauses) instead of activeDuration.

heroPaceLabel (production) has the identical guard (>100 m, >10 s) and formatter call but uses wall-clock duration, so the pace the user sees includes paused time while this unpaused version is never shown.

units.does: Formats robustMaxSpeedKmh in mph (imperial, ÷1.609344) or km/h (metric/auto) with 1 fraction digit; nil when no robust speed.
reads: ud:fitness.unitsPreference (App Group suite SharedUserDefaults.appGroup, legacy .standard fallback)

branches.effect: nil: returns nil; else continues to unit switch.
returns km/h string; .auto is unreachable because UnitsPreference.resolved never returns .auto (UnitsPreference.swift:26-29), kept for exhaustiveness.

flags.text: No caller anywhere in the repo (production or tests). The hero comment says max speed lives in the detailed cards further down, but no card renders it, so the 95th-percentile max-speed logic is never shown.

FitnessPostSummaryView comment claims 'max speed, RMSSD, METs, calories live in the detailed cards further down'; maxSpeedDisplay/avgMETsDisplay/estimatedCaloriesDisplay have no callers and derivedMetricsCard shows only a calorie rate.

units.does: 95th-percentile moving speed in km/h: converts each sample's paceSecPerKm > 0 to km/h, keeps ≥ 1.4 km/h, sorts, drops values above the sport ceiling, returns element at index floor((n−1)×0.95); nil when no samples or none survive.

branches.effect: true: maps to 3600/pace km/h; false: sample dropped.
empty: returns nil (all samples paused/implausible); else returns percentile element.

flags.text: Only caller is maxSpeedDisplay, which has no callers.

units.does: Sport-specific plausible top speed in km/h: 14 walk/hike/treadmill, 28 run/trailRun, 80 bike/indoorBike, 50 otherwise (nil sport, row, airBike, crossFit).

flags.text: Only reached via robustMaxSpeedKmh → maxSpeedDisplay, which has no callers.

units.does: Peak heart rate across samples as localized '<n> bpm'; nil when no samples or no sample carries HR.

branches.cond: samples present and at least one non-nil heartRate

flags.text: Only caller is ViewSnapshotTests.testDerivedDisplayStrings; no production caller.

units.does: Mean of positive cadenceStepsPerMin values rounded to Int, as localized '<n> spm'; nil when no samples or no positive cadence. Unlike the cadence chart it applies no sport cap / tail-spike filter.

branches.effect: empty: nil; else the average string.

flags.text: Only caller is ViewSnapshotTests.testDerivedDisplayStrings; no production caller.

units.does: Finds the split with the lowest averagePaceSecPerKm (>0) among ≥ 2 stored splits and returns (pace formatted per units preference, caption '<km|mi symbol> <index>[ · <avgHR> bpm]'); unit symbol chosen by split distance > 1500 m ⇒ miles.
reads: ud:fitness.unitsPreference (App Group suite SharedUserDefaults.appGroup, legacy .standard fallback)

branches.effect: false: nil (single-split sessions get no best-split tile).

true: 'mi' symbol; false: 'km' symbol. The label follows the split length recorded at the time, while the pace string follows the current units preference, so a session recorded in km splits viewed after switching to imperial shows 'km 3' beside a '/mi' pace.
nil HR: caption has no ' · N bpm' suffix (fallback '').

flags.text: Caption unit symbol is chosen from the stored split length (>1500 m ⇒ mi) while the pace string follows the current units preference; splits are cut at record time from the units then in force (WorkoutRecoveryService.swift:59, FitnessPostSummaryView+Share.swift:481), so after switching units the production BEST SPLIT tile shows e.g. '/mi' pace with a 'km 3' caption.

units.does: Mean of samples' METs formatted '%.1f' in the app locale; nil when no samples or no METs.

flags.text: No caller anywhere in the repo (production or tests).

units.does: Estimated kcal = avgMETs × 3.5 × bodyWeightKg × activeMinutes / 200, body weight from settings (75 kg fallback inside effectiveBodyWeightKg), formatted as rounded kcal; nil when no samples, no duration or no METs.

flags.text: No caller anywhere in the repo (production or tests).

ThresholdCards.calorieRateRow (the one shown in production) computes kcal/h = avgMETs × weight (1 MET = 1 kcal/kg/h) from UserSettingsBridge, whereas this uses METs×3.5×kg/200 per minute (=1.05 kcal/kg/h) from settingsManager — two calorie formulas and two weight sources.

units.does: X-axis domain for time-series charts: 0 … max(1, last sample offset minutes).

HR chart card: maps samples with HR to (minutes, bpm), reads the user's effective max HR, and wraps either the zone-banded HR chart (≥ 2 points) or 'No HR samples captured.' in chartShell titled 'Heart Rate'.
Swift Charts chart of zone RectangleMarks plus a monotone LineMark per HR point, leading Y axis with grid, Y domain from hrChartDomain, X domain from chartXDomain, 150 pt high.
Emits one RectangleMark per HR zone spanning first…last point minutes and the zone's lo…hi bpm, filled with the zone colour.

branches.effect: empty: xEnd 0 (unreachable for the same reason).

units.does: Returns five (lo, hi, colour) zone bands at 50/60/70/80/90 % of userMax, the top band ending at userMax+10, with increasing opacity.
Pace chart card: converts samples to pace points and wraps paceChartBody in chartShell titled 'Pace (<min/km|min/mi>)'.
reads: ud:fitness.unitsPreference (App Group suite SharedUserDefaults.appGroup, legacy .standard fallback)

units.does: Renders simpleLineChart (tint primary, 140 pt) with paceDomain Y scale and leading grid axis when ≥ 2 points, else 'Not enough movement for a pace chart.'.
Static AxisContent: leading AxisMarks with grid line and value label.

flags.text: Identical to elevationYAxis and to the inline chartYAxis block in hrChart.

units.does: Maps samples to (minutes, pace in min/km or min/mi) keeping only paceSecPerKm > 0 and equivalent speed strictly between 1 and 40 km/h.
reads: ud:fitness.unitsPreference (App Group suite SharedUserDefaults.appGroup, legacy .standard fallback)

branches.effect: false: sample dropped (very slow jitter, and any bike speed ≥ 40 km/h).

flags.text: Fixed 40 km/h ceiling regardless of sport drops every fast bike sample from the pace chart, while the same file allows 80 km/h for bikes in sportSpeedCeiling.

units.does: Monotone single-series line chart over (minutes, value) points identified by their x value, X scaled to chartXDomain, given tint and height.
Power chart card: (minutes, watts) for samples with powerWatts > 0; simpleLineChart (yellow, 140 pt) when ≥ 2 points, else 'No power data.', inside chartShell 'Running Power (W)'.

flags.text: Card is titled 'Running Power (W)' and documented as foot-pod-only, but powerWatts is also filled from Cycling Power Service meters and Concept2 rowers, and the summary shows the card for any session with power, so bike and row sessions get a 'Running Power' chart.

units.does: Cadence chart card: (minutes, cadence) for cadence > 0, filtered by filterCadence with the session sport (walk if nil); simpleLineChart (purple) when ≥ 2 points else 'No cadence data.', inside chartShell 'Cadence (spm)'.

flags.text: Title is always 'Cadence (spm)' although for bike/indoorBike/airBike the values are RPM and for row strokes/min, as cadenceCap's own comment says.

units.does: Drops points above the sport cadence cap; if ≥ 20 remain, additionally truncates at the first tail spike via truncatingTailSpike, else returns the capped list.

branches.effect: false: returns capped unchanged; true: returns tail-spike-truncated list.

units.does: Per-sport cadence ceiling: walk/hike 125, run/trailRun 220, treadmill 220, bike/indoorBike/airBike 140, row 60, crossFit 60.

branches.effect: 220 (treadmill can be walked, so a walking treadmill session gets no walk cap)

flags.text: Doc comment says run/trail-run tops at ~210 but the cap is 220.

units.does: Takes suspect tail = min(15, n/4) samples, computes the median of up to 30 preceding samples, and truncates the series at the first tail sample ≥ 1.5× that median (dropping it and everything after); otherwise returns input.

branches.effect: empty: returns capped unchanged — unreachable, the only caller passes ≥ 20 points so baselineEnd ≥ 15.
true: median = mean of two middle values; false: middle value.
first match: returns prefix before it; no match: falls through to return capped.

flags.text: guard !baselineValues.isEmpty can never fail: filterCadence only calls with count ≥ 20, giving a baseline of ≥ 15 values.

units.does: Card container: VStack with semibold secondary-coloured title and the content, padded 14, full width, card background, 14 pt continuous rounded clip.
Caption-sized tertiary-coloured Text for empty chart states.
HR Y domain: 40…max(userMax,160) when no points; else lower=max(40,min−10), upper=max(lower+10, min(userMax+10, max+10)).

branches.effect: empty: 40…max(userMax,160) (unreachable from hrChart, which needs ≥ 2 points).

flags.text: upper is capped at userMax+10, so any genuine HR more than 10 bpm above effectiveMaxHR (which falls back to Tanaka or 180 when the user never entered one) lies outside the explicit Y domain and the top of the HR line is drawn off-scale instead of the axis growing to fit.

units.does: Pace Y domain padded by max(0.1, 10 % of range) each side, floored at 0, not inverted (faster plots lower); 0…20 when empty.

branches.effect: empty: 0…20 (unreachable from paceChartBody, which needs ≥ 2 points).

units.does: Elevation card: picks mi/ft (imperial) or km/m labels, builds elevationPoints, sets max X to max(last GPS cumulative distance, stored distanceMeters scaled), and renders title 'Elevation (<unit>)' plus elevationChart in a padded rounded card.
reads: ud:fitness.unitsPreference (App Group suite SharedUserDefaults.appGroup, legacy .standard fallback)

branches.effect: true: miles symbol; false: km symbol.
true: feet symbol; false: metres symbol.

flags.text: Comment on distanceScale says the x-domain is clamped to the covered distance to avoid dead space past the data, but the code takes max(GPS-cumulative distance, stored distance), so whenever stored distanceMeters exceeds the GPS cumulative distance the axis extends past the last point.
Re-implements chartShell's card styling inline (padding 14, card background, 14 pt rounded) instead of calling chartShell.

units.does: Converts elevationSeries(track) (km, m) into display units: distance back to metres then × distanceScale (mi or km), altitude × feetPerMeter when imperial.
Renders an indexed Chart of AreaMark+LineMark per elevation point with X 0…max(0.1,maxX), leading grid Y axis, 140 pt high, when ≥ 2 points; else 'Not enough GPS fixes for an elevation chart.'.
Leading AxisMarks with grid line and value label for the elevation chart.

flags.text: Identical to leadingGridAxis.

units.does: HRR stop reference time: session.endDate, else startDate + last sample offset, else startDate.

branches.cond: endDate present / last sample present (?? chain)
branches.effect: endDate nil: startDate + last sample offset; no samples either: startDate.

units.does: True when hrrSamples is nil and more than 150 s (120 window + 30 grace) have passed since hrrStopDate, using Date() at evaluation time.

flags.text: AppFactResolver.postStopHRRWindowOpen re-implements the same rule (hrrSamples == nil within hrrCaptureWindowSec + hrrWriteGraceSec of the end) with its own reference date (archive entry endDate, no sample-offset fallback), so assistant and summary can disagree for sessions without an endDate.

units.does: While hrrSamples is nil, renders a 1 Hz TimelineView starting at hrrStopDate whose content is hrrCountdownTick; renders nothing once samples are stored.

flags.text: The banner condition is only hrrSamples == nil, not hrrNeverCaptured, so for every old or imported session without HRR the 1 Hz TimelineView keeps re-evaluating forever while rendering nothing.

units.does: Computes remaining = 120 − seconds since stop and renders the countdown row only while remaining > 0.
units.entry: Invoked from hrrCaptureBanner's TimelineView content closure once per second by SwiftUI's periodic timeline schedule.

branches.effect: true: countdown row; false: nothing (banner disappears after the window even if no samples ever arrive).

units.does: Banner row: heart icon, countdown text, tinted background with accent stroke, 12 pt rounded.
Two texts: 'Keep your strap on for M:SS more' and an explanation that HRR drops at +1/+2 min from peak are being captured.

flags.text: Banner text tells the user the drops are measured 'from peak', but the HRR card measures every drop from HR at Stop (stopReferencedDrop), per its own comment.

units.does: Formats seconds as 'M:SS'.

flags.text: Same as formatDuration's sub-hour branch and the inline '%d:%02d' in hrrCountdownChip.

units.does: HRR card: derives captureFinished (samples stored or never-captured timeout), captureFailed (finished and samples nil/empty) and the stop-referenced 1-minute drop, then stacks header, HR-at-stop row, value row and narrative in a 16 pt rounded card.

branches.effect: nil: treated as empty, so captureFailed = captureFinished; a never-captured session (nil after timeout) shows 'no signal'.

flags.text: captureFinished is computed from Date() only when this card's body is evaluated; the countdown chip's TimelineView redraws only its own content. If the recorder never writes samples back (app suspended, failed write) and nothing else invalidates the parent view, the chip stays at 'capturing · 0:00' with a spinner and the 'keep the strap on' narrative indefinitely, which is what hrrNeverCaptured was added to prevent.

The card recomputes the drop from hrAtStop (last sample HR within 15 s of the final sample) while the stored drop, shown by hrrSentence, the Fitness tab mean and CSV, uses the recorder's live currentHR at Stop; the two stop-HR sources can differ, so one session can show two different 1-minute HRR numbers.
No test exercises hrrCard or its helpers (hrAtStop, stopReferencedDrop, hrrNeverCaptured, hrrStatusChip); ViewSnapshotTests covers only the chart/elevation cards and derived strings.

units.does: Header row: heart icon, 'HEART RATE RECOVERY' caption, spacer, status chip.
HR at Stop: heartRate of the last sample with HR whose offset is within 15 s of the final sample offset; nil if none or ≤ 0.

branches.cond: a qualifying tail sample with HR > 0

units.does: Displayed drop for one HRR reading: hrAtStop − sample.hr, except healthKitComputed readings or when hrAtStop is nil, which return the stored sample.drop (itself stopHR − hr, computed from the recorder's currentHR at Stop, HRRCaptureService.swift:183).

branches.effect: true: stop-referenced drop; false: stored drop.

flags.text: HRRSample.drop is documented as 'Drop from peak HR' and peakHR as the reference peak, but the capture service fills both with HR at Stop; readers of the model (and this unit's comment) rely on the wrong meaning.

units.does: Shows 'HR at stop: N bpm' when hrAtStop exists, else nothing.
Two value blocks: 1-minute reading (good ≥ 12, ok ≥ 8) and 2-minute reading (good ≥ 22, ok ≥ 16).

Narrative under the HRR card: graded narrative for the stop-referenced 1-minute drop; else 'keep the strap on' while capturing; else 'wasn't captured' for nil; else 'couldn't be captured' for an empty array.

branches.effect: shows 'couldn't be captured'. When samples exist but none within 60±10 s, no branch matches and nothing is rendered.

flags.text: When capture finished with a non-empty hrrSamples array but none within 60±10 s (e.g. only a 2-minute reading), no narrative renders and hrrStatusChip also renders nothing, leaving a card with '— not yet' placeholders and no explanation.

units.does: Status chip: countdown chip while capturing, orange 'no signal' when failed, else graded label coloured by 12/8 thresholds for the 1-minute drop; nothing when finished with no 1-minute drop.

branches.effect: 'no signal' (also shown for the nil/never-captured case).

units.does: 1 Hz TimelineView chip showing spinner and 'capturing · M:SS' remaining until hrrStopDate+120 s, clamped at 0, with an accessibility label.
Quality word for a 1-minute drop: ≥ 18 excellent, ≥ 12 strong, ≥ 8 ok, else slower.
Narrative sentence for a 1-minute drop with the same 18/12/8 bands.

flags.text: hrrSentence (and WorkoutPDFReport.hrrSentences) grade the same 18/12/8 bands with different wording, on the stored drop rather than the card's stopReferencedDrop.

units.does: Value block: uppercased label then either the reading or the '— not yet' placeholder.

flags.text: The placeholder always says 'not yet', including after the capture finished or failed and for a missing 2-minute reading, implying data is still coming when it never will.

units.does: Reading: stop-referenced drop in large scaled font coloured by thresholds, 'bpm', and the provenance label.
Placeholder: large '—' and caption 'not yet'.
Colour for a drop: green ≥ good, amber ≥ ok, else orange.
Metres → miles (÷1609.344) or km (÷1000) scale factor.
Chart content for one elevation point: translucent accent AreaMark plus catmull-Rom accent LineMark at (distance, altitude).
Caption-styled secondary-colour Text that wraps vertically.
Cumulative-distance elevation series from GPS fixes: for each fix, cumulative CLLocation distance (km) and raw altitude (m); empty for < 2 fixes.

branches.effect: adds distance from previous fix; first fix stays at 0.

flags.text: The type comment says the share sheet reaches elevationSeries through a forwarder, but the forwarder FitnessPostSummaryView.elevationSeries has no callers anywhere; the only caller is elevationPoints in this file.

Plots CLLocation.altitude unfiltered: no verticalAccuracy or missing-altitude check. GPX imports without <ele> get altitude 0 (GPXImporter.swift:120) and polyline decodes with fewer altitudes than coordinates get 0 (GPXExporter.swift:150), so the elevation card shows a flat sea-level line or a cliff to 0 m as real terrain.

units.does: Provenance caption: strap → 'from strap', watchSamples → 'via Apple Watch', healthKitComputed → 'via Apple Health'.

flags.text: Comment says the share sheet reaches hrrProvenanceLabel through a forwarder; FitnessPostSummaryView.hrrProvenanceLabel (and the hrrNarrative forwarder) have no callers, so both forwarders are dead.
